svg.title: The two halves of a Slutsky argument for the studentized mean
svg.desc: Left panel: the density of the sample standard deviation divided by sigma collapses onto one as n grows from 5 to 200. Right panel: the studentized mean of a normal sample has heavy t tails at n = 5 and sits on the standard normal by n = 30. Three boxes below assemble the product.
svg.text: Slutsky's theorem, one factor at a time
The studentized mean is a product: root n times (xbar minus mu) over sigma, times sigma over S. The first
factor goes to a standard normal in distribution, the second to the constant 1 in probability, and Slutsky
says the product goes to a standard normal. Both panels are drawn for a normal population.
the ratio settles on the normal
The constant limit in the second factor is not decoration: two sequences that merely converge in
distribution can combine into anything at all.
